title: MoCL: Metabolic Optimization for Curvature-Aware Continual Learning
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: A two-part pipeline builds a factorized subspace from layer statistics, then uses entropy-based gating to project and correct gradients, balancing stability and plasticity.
layout: 2 stacked dashed panels, left-to-right flow, matrix heatmaps as visual motif
description: The figure has two stacked dashed-border panels with yellow title tags. The top panel, 'Tsallis Entropic Metabolic Gating', runs left to right. A blue-orange gradient heatmap G is combined with a factorized subspace sketch of two crossing planes, then projected into a projected gradient G-hat. A second row takes Kronecker factors E_A and E_G to an energy map, then a sigmoid metabolic gating curve, then gated energy. The two rows merge at a reconstruction node that gives a corrected gradient. A protected/available gradient decomposition bar sits above it. A weight cube W_{t-1} leads to W_t, then to a loss landscape contour plot showing convergence. The bottom panel, 'Factorized Subspace Approximation', shows forward and backward passes through Layer Weight W_l. Covariance matrices C_A (red) and C_G (blue) go through EVD and incremental SVD, giving the subspaces U_A and U_G. Blue and red color-code the two factors, with equations under the arrows.
caption: Overview of MoCL. To mitigate forgetting, MoCL employs the Tsallis entropy metabolic gating Gq to modulate gradient
abstract: Continual learning requires models to mitigate catastrophic forgetting of prior knowledge while learning a sequence of tasks. Although existing methods based on orthogonal projection prevent interference by constraining parameter updates, they tend to limit plasticity as the task sequence progresses. The reliance on the linear approximation further causes the projected gradients to deviate from the nonlinear manifold. To address these issues, we propose Metabolic Optimization for Continual Learning (MoCL), a rehearsal-free framework that strikes a balance between stability and plasticity. To capture the geometric manifold of prior knowledge, MoCL introduces a factorized subspace approximation that avoids expensive explicit matrix inversion. Given the heavy-tailed distribution of the Fisher Information Matrix, we employ a metabolic gating based on Tsallis entropy to suppress updates that conflict with historical knowledge. Theoretical and empirical analyses show that MoCL suppresses interference while supporting shared low-loss behavior across sequential tasks. Extensive experimental results across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that MoCL outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both classification performance and efficiency.
